identity.title: AGN feeding and feedback in Fornax A. Kinematical analysis of the multi-phase ISM

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using MeerKAT, ALMA and MUSE observations we reveal a complex distribution of the atomic (H I), molecular (CO), and ionised gas in its centre and along the radio jets.

evidence.quote: at the assumed distance of 20.8 Mpc

question.value: How do the multi-phase gas kinematics in Fornax A reveal concurrent AGN feeding (Chaotic Cold Accretion) and feedback (outflows)?

evidence.quote: We aim to understand if and how the cold and ionised gas have triggered the nuclear activities in the last $3$ Myr, and what are the feedback effects resulting from these.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00129.S.

sensitivity.value: 12 mJy/beam per channel (9.9 km/s); 3 sigma surface brightness limit 0.33 Msun/pc2

evidence.quote: The noise in the datacube is $12$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ per channel ($\Delta v\sim9.9$$\,$km s$^{-1}$).
We observed Fornax A with MeerKAT (cite: Jonas:2016; Camilo:2018) in two different commissioning observations in June 2018.

analysis_steps.goal: make CO cube and moment maps at H I resolution

method.value: New CO(1-0) cube at same resolution as H I; SoFiA used for moment maps

evidence.quote: We create the total CO (1–0)  image, velocity field and velocity-dispersion field using `SoFiA`, analogously to what done for the H I.
assuming a Galactic CO (1–0) -to-H$_{\,2}$ conversion factor $X_2=4.3$${\rm M}_\odot$(K $\,$km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{-2}$)$^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: classify cold gas kinematics with rotation model and k-plot

method.value: Schematic rotating disk plus expanding ring model; spectra matching model for at least 50% of the zero-intensity width are 'rotating'; remaining points clustered in k-plot (width vs centroid) into R1-R6

evidence.quote: We define as ‘rotating’, every spectrum of the \[N II\]$\lambda$6583 datacube whose fitted emission line matches the model line for at least $50\%$ of its full-width at zero intensity.

key_parameters.value: inner disk i=89 deg, PA=-30 deg, v_rot=340 km/s; ring v_exp=2000 km/s; dispersion 35 km/s

evidence.loc: 6.1 Modelling the kinematics of the ISM
evidence.quote: we do not constrain all the parameters of the model with an automated fit.

analysis_steps.goal: derive masses, Taylor number, C-ratio, outflow properties

method.value: Masses per region (H2 from CO), Ta_t=v_rot/sigma_3D, C=t_cool/t_eddy, outflow mass and power from R1, R5, R6

evidence.quote: we use the masses of the H I, CO and ionised gas in regions $R1$, $R5$ and $R6$ (see Table [1](#tab:masses)) to determine the total mass of the outflow $M_{\rm out}\sim 2\times10^7$ ${\rm M}_\odot$.

evidence.quote: Assuming that the outflow was ejected at the same time of the jets, the mass outflow rate is $\dot{M}_{\rm OUT}\sim 5$ ${\rm M}_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Cold gas (H I and CO) follows the dust and shows high dispersion in the wake of the jets and in the outer ring

evidence.quote: In both phases of the gas, the highest dispersion is found where the radio jets bend in the NW and, more evidently in the SE.

claims.hypothesis: Is the outer ring an outflow rather than rotation?
claims.experiment: Compare MUSE, H I and CO velocity fields with rotation/expansion models
claims.result: Ring terminal velocities along short axis, ~2000 km/s expansion if radial
claims.finding: Outer ring is a multi-phase outflow of ~2e7 Msun

evidence.quote: we identify an entrained massive ($\sim$ $10^7$ ${\rm M}_\odot$) multi-phase outflow ($v_{\rm OUT}\sim 2000$ $\,$km s$^{-1}$).

claims.hypothesis: Is gas in the EW-stripe undergoing CCA?
claims.result: EW-stripe consistent with CCA expectations, C-ratio approaching unity
claims.finding: CCA likely ongoing, feeding the AGN

evidence.quote: show that CCA is very likely on-going within the EW-stripe.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: EW-stripe as edge-on circumnuclear disk rejected: redshifted on east without blueshifted west counterpart

evidence.quote: The stripe has redshifted velocities in the east but does not show a blueshifted counterpart in the west.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA and MeerKAT broad wings often below S/N~3; w80 inferred from Gaussian dispersion

evidence.quote: the shallow broad wings that dominate $w80$ are often seen below the $S/N\sim3$, making uncertain a direct measurement of the full extent of the lines.

referee_caveats_inferred: Kinematic model is schematic, not fitted; no uncertainties on masses or outflow quantities
Poor spatial resolution of ALMA data limits k-plot statistics
Outflow velocity of 2000 km/s hinges on assumed low ring inclination
